glucose_high.title: Manage Blood Sugar
glucose_high.detail: Your glucose is elevated. Reduce refined carbs, sugary beverages, and white rice. Eat more fiber-rich foods and check levels regularly.

hba1c_high.title: HbA1c Requires Attention
hba1c_high.detail: A raised HbA1c suggests poor long-term glucose control. Consult a doctor for a diabetes management plan.

systolic_bp_high.title: Lower Blood Pressure
systolic_bp_high.detail: High systolic BP strains the heart. Reduce sodium (<2g/day), increase potassium, limit caffeine, and manage stress.

diastolic_bp_high.title: Diastolic BP Elevated
diastolic_bp_high.detail: Elevated diastolic pressure increases stroke risk. Follow the DASH diet, exercise regularly, and reduce alcohol intake.

bmi_high.title: Weight Management Needed
bmi_high.detail: Excess weight raises risk for diabetes and heart disease. Aim for a 500 kcal daily deficit through diet and 150 min exercise per week.

cholesterol_high.title: Reduce Total Cholesterol
cholesterol_high.detail: Cut saturated fats and trans fats. Increase soluble fiber (oats, beans) and omega-3 fatty acids (fish, flaxseeds).

ldl_high.title: LDL "Bad" Cholesterol High
ldl_high.detail: Elevated LDL accelerates plaque build-up in arteries. Avoid fried foods, increase plant sterols, and consider a statin if advised by your doctor.

hdl_low.title: Raise HDL "Good" Cholesterol
hdl_low.detail: Low HDL means less cholesterol removal from arteries. Exercise aerobically, quit smoking, eat healthy fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts).

triglycerides_high.title: High Triglycerides
triglycerides_high.detail: Excess sugar and alcohol raises triglycerides. Limit sugar, refined carbs, and alcohol. Eat more omega-3s and increase physical activity.

heart_rate_high.title: Elevated Resting Heart Rate
heart_rate_high.detail: A resting heart rate above 100 bpm can signal stress or cardiovascular strain. Practice deep breathing, stay hydrated, and reduce caffeine.

creatinine_high.title: Kidney Function Concern
creatinine_high.detail: Raised creatinine may indicate reduced kidney function. Stay well hydrated, avoid NSAIDs, control blood pressure, and get a kidney function panel.

waist_cm_high.title: Excess Abdominal Fat
waist_cm_high.detail: Central obesity increases heart and diabetes risk. Reduce refined carbs, alcohol, and add core-strengthening exercises.

sleep_hours_low.title: Improve Sleep Quality
sleep_hours_low.detail: Sleeping under 6 hours raises cortisol, blood pressure, and insulin resistance. Aim for 7–9 hours with a consistent sleep schedule.

stress_level_high.title: Reduce Chronic Stress
stress_level_high.detail: Chronic stress elevates cortisol and blood pressure. Try mindfulness, yoga, 20-min daily walks, journaling, or speaking with a therapist.

smoking_active.title: Quit Smoking — #1 Priority
smoking_active.detail: Smoking doubles heart disease risk and directly damages lungs and blood vessels. Use NRT patches or medication to quit.

alcohol_heavy.title: Reduce Alcohol Intake
alcohol_heavy.detail: Heavy drinking raises blood pressure, triglycerides, and liver risk. Limit to ≤1 drink/day (women) or ≤2/day (men).

exercise_low.title: Increase Physical Activity
exercise_low.detail: Less than 2 active days/week significantly raises disease risk. Start with 30-minute walks 5x/week, add resistance training twice a week.

family_history.title: Monitor Due to Family History
family_history.detail: Genetic predisposition raises your baseline risk. Get annual check-ups including lipid panel, glucose, and blood pressure.

diabetes_risk.title: Diabetes Risk Detected
diabetes_risk.detail: Your profile matches pre-diabetic or diabetic patterns. Request an HbA1c and fasting glucose test. Early lifestyle changes can reverse pre-diabetes.

heart_risk.title: Cardiovascular Risk Elevated
heart_risk.detail: Multiple cardiac risk markers are raised. Consider a lipid panel, ECG, and stress test. Prioritize cholesterol control and blood pressure.

hypertension_risk.title: Hypertension Risk
hypertension_risk.detail: Your blood pressure pattern suggests hypertension. Monitor BP twice daily for 2 weeks and consult a doctor. The DASH diet can reduce SBP by up to 11 mmHg.

kidney_risk.title: Kidney Health Concern
kidney_risk.detail: Markers suggest kidney stress. Drink 2–3 L of water daily, avoid excessive protein supplements, and control BP and blood sugar.

see_doctor.title: Consult a Healthcare Professional
see_doctor.detail: Your overall risk profile is elevated. A comprehensive health screening with blood work, physical exam, and specialist referral is strongly recommended.

healthy.title: Maintain Your Healthy Lifestyle
healthy.detail: Your parameters are within healthy ranges. Continue regular exercise, a balanced diet, adequate sleep, and annual health check-ups.
